text:
elin: Heads up — we hit failed scale-ups in eu-west-1 during the morning load test. Autoscaler kept saying 'no capacity' even though we have spare spot nodegroups.
tyler: ugh. any error from the autoscaler logs? can you paste the snippet?
elin: here's the relevant bit from the CA logs:
```
I0324 09:12:05.123456 1 scale_up.go:348] NodeGroup my-gpu-spot-eu: there are 3 pending pods unschedulable due to resource limits
I0324 09:12:05.123789 1 scale_up.go:372] No candidates found: node group my-gpu-spot-eu has insufficient IP addresses
```
rafi: insufficient IPs — sounds like subnet IP exhaustion / ENI quota problem. We saw this with dense GPU nodes before.
sophia: yeah, big GPUs use large instance types and allocate a lot of ENIs. region subnets in eu-west-1 are at 90%.
tyler: did the terraform module set `max_pods` or CNI configs? we usually set `max_pods` via kubelet args so node allocatable isn't oversized.
elin: terraform uses our module `modules/nodepool/gpu-module` — snippet:
```
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_spot" {
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge"]
  scaling_config { desired_size = 0; min_size = 0; max_size = 10 }
  labels = { "workload" = "inference" }
  taints = [{ key = "gpu-only", value = "true", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]
}
```
rafi: p4d is massive, ENI count per instance is large. Our subnet (/24) only had ~240 usable addresses and we try to land several pods with `hostNetwork: false` and lots of pods per node.
sophia: also saw CA failing because the nodegroup has `mixedInstancesPolicy` for spot + on-demand but the IAM role used by cluster-autoscaler only had describe/stream autoscaling on the ASG not the EC2 permissions for ENIs. CA needs `ec2:DescribeInstances` to compute IP availability.
tyler: can we fix in two parts: 1) quick mitigation in Helm values for cluster-autoscaler to set `--expander=least-waste` and `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` and 2) terraform change to ensure subnets have extra CIDR or use secondary ENIs / use smaller instance types for denser packing?
elin: +1. For immediate relief I spun up a small ondemand nodepool with `g4dn.xlarge` using terraform to absorb pods while we sort ENIs.

deploy-bot: deploy started: helm upgrade --install cluster-autoscaler infra/cluster-autoscaler -f values/ca-eu-west1.yaml

typer: typo: @tyler sorry about earlier
tyler: no worries.
rafi: proposing a longer-term automation change: update our nodepool module to accept `preferred_instance_families` and a flag `prefers_smaller_instances` so we can prefer multiple smaller GPUs instead of one huge instance in constrained subnets. Also add outputs for `eni_per_instance` calculated from instance type mapping so TF can warn.
sophia: love that. also add a test in CI that simulates IP exhaustion: spin up a nodegroup in a throwaway VPC with /28 and assert terraform plan shows the subnet capacity warning.
elin: for CA helm values I used:
```
extraArgs:
  scale-down-unneeded-time: "10m"
  expander: "least-waste"
  skip-nodes-with-system-pods: false
rbac:
  create: true
autoscaler:
  aws:
    skip-nodes-with-local-storage: false
```

rafi: we should also add an alert that fires when `kube_node_status_capacity{resource="pods"}` usage exceeds 85% per-subnet to catch before CA complains.
tyler: and in terraform add `subnet_auto_expand = true`? can't for existing subnets. But we can add a module to provision a sibling /24 and update route tables — automated in tf plan with a prompt.
elsin: small nit: name is elin ;) 

elin: action items I'll own:
- push helm value change to infra helm repo (PR today) — short-term CA tweak
- add on-demand fallback nodepool TF (small gpu types) and a flag so it's created only when `allow_burst_pool = true`
- open ticket to add `eni_per_instance` mapping + warning in nodepool module

rafi: I'll add the Prometheus alert + dashboard panel for subnet pod capacity.
sophia: I'll prototype the CI test for subnet exhaustion.
tyler: agree on docs update for runbooks: what to do when CA reports insufficient IP addresses — link the PR after it lands.
elin: thanks. reassigning follow-ups. If anyone's going to touch TF module, ping me for a quick sync on naming conventions.

deploy-bot: release succeeded: cluster-autoscaler v1.23.0 -> v1.23.1 (values from elin).
